summary: Retries produce duplicate tool calls due to ephemeral nonce encoding differences across Python/TS/Go SDKs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reporting duplicate external tool/webhook invocations when client library retries occur mid-stream. Behavior appears only when clients are using a mix of Python and TypeScript SDKs behind an edge proxy.

Impact:
- Duplicate downstream charges for webhook recipients (MapleHealth integration).
- Partial data duplication in downstream systems; high business impact for patient-scheduling flows.
- Reproducible for customer request flows that include function/tool calling and a short lived ephemeral nonce placed in request headers.

Environment:
- MapleHealth Dedicated deployment in us-east-1.
- Redwood Dedicated pool (g5-2x), private VPC peering.
- SDK versions observed: python-sdk v2.9.1, ts-sdk v3.0.2, go-sdk not used by customer but reproduced by Support.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Create a streaming chat session that requests a tool/webhook call (function_call).
2) The client attaches X-Redwood-Nonce header generated by local session code (ephemeral 24-byte nonce, base64 encoded).
3) Trigger a simulated network hiccup: client network drops and reconnects, SDK retry logic replays in-flight events.
4) Downstream observes duplicate webhook POSTs (same payload, different Redwood request IDs).

Observed behavior:
- When the request is retried by TS SDK the nonce header is URL-encoded by the edge-sidecar (plus EOL normalization). Python client sends a raw base64 string. Edge proxy normalizes whitespace/EOL resulting in two different canonical header values across paths; our idempotency normalization path treats them as distinct, so server-side dedupe fails.

Expected behavior:
- Header canonicalization should be consistent across SDKs and proxies such that retries referencing the same logical nonce are deduplicated and tool calls are not duplicated.

Logs & artifacts attached:
- Customer captured request traces (request IDs): r-20260310-82A, r-20260310-82B
- Edge proxy config dump and header rewrite rules (anonymized) attached to ticket.
- Minimal repro scripts from Support for Python and TS included in comments.

Workaround (customer):
- Customer temporarily added a server-side dedupe that hashes normalized JSON body + timestamp window (not ideal).
- Suggested temporary mitigation: client-side avoid mixing SDKs for same session or ensure nonce encoding canonicalization (URL-safe base64) on all clients.

Requested outcome:
- Guidance on canonical nonce encoding and recommended header normalization rules for SDKs and edge proxies.
- Bugfix or doc update to prevent future interop duplicates.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:22 - Aisha Kumar: Filed on behalf of MapleHealth. Provided initial traces and edge proxy rewrite config. Customer reports duplicate webhook POSTs correlated to retry events.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Support Engineer (Aisha): Reproduced locally with python-sdk v2.9.1 against edge-sidecar v1.14. Noticed base64 vs url-safe base64 differences after proxy rewrite. Opening investigation with SDK and edge teams. CC @#support @#edge-proxy.
2026-03-10 14:30 - Customer (MapleHealth SRE, Jonah Lee): We can confirm switching TS client to url-safe base64 reduced dupes but still saw a few. Happy to share repro credentials in DM.

2026-03-11 08:45 - Diego Morales (Edge Team): Observed edge-sidecar had a header normalization feature enabled for HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation that converts plus signs to spaces on EOL boundaries in our environment. Filing INT-2203 to track patch. Tentative root cause: EOL normalization + header canonicalization difference between SDKs leads to failing idempotency key match.

2026-03-11 10:10 - SDK Lead (Priya Shah): Confirmed python-sdk currently emits standard base64 with padding while TS SDK team adopted url-safe base64 in v3.0.x. We need an SDK compatibility note and possibly normalize encoding in client and server layer. Patch PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/7890 (adds url-safe base64 helper and tests).

2026-03-12 09:00 - Diego Morales: Added replication notes: reproduced using go-sdk as well when explicitly toggling encoding to standard base64. Edge proxy rewrite rule reproduced behavior with header chunking enabled on HTTP/2.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Nonce encoding mismatch (standard base64 vs url-safe base64) across SDKs causes different canonical header values after proxy header normalization.

Hypothesis 2: Edge proxy is performing EOL/whitespace normalization when mapping HTTP/2 header blocks to HTTP/1 downstream which corrupts '+' padding characters, turning them into spaces in certain chunk boundaries.

Reproduction steps performed by Support: run python repro that emits X-Redwood-Nonce=SGVsbG8rK3BhZGRpbmc= then pass through edge-sidecar with HTTP/2 chunk size 8192 -> observe server receives 'SGVsbG8 K3BhZGRpbmc='.
Captured pcap between client->edge shows header split across two HEADERS frames; HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translator glues back and applies linearization causing '+'->space.
Edge team confirmed config flag 'http2_strip_trailing_padding' toggles behavior. Disabling for MapleHealth eliminated observed space substitution in test env.
SDK teams agreed to document canonical nonce encoding: use url-safe base64 (RFC 4648 section 5) without padding for header tokens to reduce exposure to '+','/' and '=' transformations.

Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/7890 to add helpers and interop tests across python/ts/go and to add a warning in README. Edge team preparing a patch to avoid whitespace normalization at proxy translation layer.
Linked internal ticket INT-2203 to track edge-sidecar config change and rollout to dedicated clusters.
next_steps: Edge team to deploy config change to MapleHealth dedicated pool in a canary region and monitor for duplicate webhook counts (INT-2203).
SDK teams to land PR #7890 and cut patch releases: python-sdk v2.9.2 and ts-sdk v3.0.3 with url-safe nonce helper and compatibility notes.
Create short KB article for customers: 'Canonical nonce encoding for idempotency headers' and link in SDK docs and support runbook.
After edge patch deploy, ask MapleHealth to toggle back to mixed SDKs and validate dedupe metrics for 48h.
